title: Navy Day in New York
photoNote: USS New York (BB-34) arrives in New York Harbor for the Navy Day fleet review, 19 October 1945. U.S. Navy color photo 80-GK-6554 (NARA 178141304), public domain. Eight days before Navy Day.
body:
Eight weeks after Japan surrendered, the warships that won the war lay at anchor in New York, and the President came to thank them.

27 October 1945. It was Navy Day, the first since the war ended, and New York turned out for the fleet. President Harry Truman spoke at the commissioning of the new carrier USS Franklin D. Roosevelt and reviewed the warships from the destroyer Renshaw. He also went aboard USS Missouri and bent down to read the plaque marking the spot where Japan had signed the surrender.

In Central Park he gave a speech carried on every radio network. America had built a navy of 1,200 warships, he said. And it held the atomic bomb.

"The possession in our hands of this new power of destruction we regard as a sacred trust," he told the crowd.

The war was over. The question of what America would do with its power had just begun.

#OnThisDay #WW2
